name: Advice Without A Way To Check It
problem: Advice and plans are given as one answer, not as the option most likely to work for this person with a metric to check it, and when the better option is unknown the AI does not propose an experiment that would settle it, though the app has an Experiments feature built for that.
who_has_it: People pursuing big goals who need to know what is most likely to work for them, not only what is plausible.
why_it_matters: What sets the product apart from a general chatbot is finding what is most likely to work for the individual and measuring it; an experiment the person carries out gives them a grounded path and the metrics to track it.
why_hard: Most likely needs evidence, the person's own history and a metric, which are rarely all present; an experiment takes the person's time and consent; and a model answers fluently whether or not it has them.
existing_attempts: Experiment tools that find, create and change a quest's experiments when the person asks; experiment generation at the end of quest creation in the host; the intent frame and specification slice for background work.

name: Wrong Or Inconsistent Representative
problem: Which AI representative handles a message, a queued task, a newly assigned goal or an autopilot pass is decided in several places by different rules, with no shared definition of the right representative, no labelled measure of how often it is right, and no rule that work spawned from a thread keeps that thread's representative. A quest can have several representatives, each with its own higher mind, so a wrong choice also grounds the request in the wrong view.
who_has_it: People and teams whose quests have more than one AI representative, and anyone who delegates work from a chat or hands a new goal to someone.
why_it_matters: In production a chat's turns ran as the person's default representative while the tasks they spawned ran as two other personas, with a different voice and different evidence in one thread, and the person called the advice inconsistent. Choosing the representative decides whose role, notes and long view ground the work.
why_hard: The fit between a request and a representative depends on roles written in free text, the quests each is assigned and what the person asked for; a bare mention of a name is not the same as asking for it; a representative may be visible to one member of a team and not another; and asking the person each time is its own failure.
existing_attempts: The host's fast-model classifier that picks among a quest's assigned representatives and falls back to the person's default; the task runner's persona resolver; the autopilot roster with per-representative days and instructions; per-viewer visibility of representatives.

name: Long-Term Goal Goes Quiet
problem: The AI answers the request in front of it and lets the person's long-term goal go quiet, so each small task is done without the end in sight; a pointer to the goal in every reply nags, hijacks a simple question or lands on a person who is in a hurry or upset.
who_has_it: Anyone using Quest AI on a quest that serves a larger intent.
why_it_matters: The assistant is meant to keep moving people forward with the end in sight, at the intent level they are working at; an assistant that does not looks like any other chat AI.
why_hard: A pointer is right at one moment and wrong at the next (urgent, narrow, unrelated, emotional, already raised), the right level depends on what the person is doing, and a pointer has to name the real next milestone and the real current reading, not an invented one.
existing_attempts: The reply voice already says to answer first and be proactive only where it is worth the person's time; no measure yet checks whether it points at the next milestone or holds back when it should.

name: Decisions Not Reaching The Person
problem: A step only a person on the quest may decide can be taken without them, reach the wrong teammate, or be dropped before they answer.
who_has_it: The person responsible for the account or quest, and teammates asked to approve.
why_it_matters: An irreversible act taken for a person erodes trust and is hard to repair, and an approval request they cannot act on is of no use to them.
why_hard: The model has to recognise a human-only step by judgment, not a word list; the request has to carry enough context to decide; a quest has several people with different roles; and the delivery path differs by host application.
existing_attempts: Confirming everything, denylists of risky words, review queues outside the assistant, and asking in free text.
